shortcut_name: direct reduction to bipartite graph coloring
evidence: deepseek-v4-flash uses `color[v] = color[u] ^ 1`; gpt-oss-120b comments `# BFS this component`; qwen3-coder states the clauses mean the endpoints cannot both be False or both True; glm-5 explicitly seeks the lexicographically smallest assignment after building `adj`.
affordance_in_statement: Each constraint is given as a pair of indices $u$ and $v$, which enforces exactly two boolean clauses that must both be satisfied: $(x_u \lor x_v)$ and $(\neg x_u \lor \neg x_v)$.
removal_suggestion: There is no semantics-preserving way to remove this affordance: the task is intrinsically graph 2-colorability. It can only be re-presented indirectly, for example by describing the allowed truth-value combinations for each pair without explicitly explaining that the endpoints must differ.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Treats every constraint as an undirected edge and solves it by BFS parity coloring.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The two clauses together prohibit equal endpoint values, yielding a standard bipartite graph.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Builds an undirected adjacency graph and performs BFS component coloring.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: Each input pair is directly usable as an undirected graph edge.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Explicitly derives that each pair requires one endpoint True and the other False, then uses graph coloring.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The statement gives both clauses $(x_u \lor x_v)$ and $(\neg x_u \lor \neg x_v)$.

survivor_shortcuts.shortcut: Constructs an adjacency graph, colors components, and selects the lexicographically preferred component orientation.
survivor_shortcuts.affordance: The constraints reduce to a two-coloring problem, with the stated 1/2 encoding determining the preferred orientation.

common_affordance: The conjunction of the two clauses is exactly the requirement that every listed pair have opposite Boolean values, so the instance is ordinary bipartite graph testing and coloring.
recommended_edit: No single semantics-preserving edit can defeat all survivors: bipartite coloring is the intrinsic core of the task. If only presentation may change, remove the explanatory pairing of the clauses and describe each constraint indirectly via its allowed truth-value combinations, but this is unlikely to defeat correct solvers.
